lessons.title: What are Articles?
lessons.description: Understand the meaning and purpose of articles in English.

sections.heading: 1. What is an Article?
sections.content: An article is a word used before a noun to indicate whether we are referring to something specific or something non-specific.

examples.explanation: A refers to a non-specific dog. The listener does not know which dog.
The refers to the specific dog already mentioned.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Articles
sections.content: English has three articles: A, An and The.

rules.name: A
rules.description: An indefinite article generally used before singular countable nouns beginning with a consonant sound.

rules.name: An
rules.description: An indefinite article generally used before singular countable nouns beginning with a vowel sound.

rules.name: The
rules.description: A definite article used when referring to a specific or identifiable noun.
rules.example: The sun, the book on the table.

sections.heading: 3. Definite and Indefinite Articles
sections.content: A and An are indefinite articles. The is a definite article.

examples.explanation: The dress is not identified specifically.
The dress is now identifiable from the context.

sections.heading: 4. Important Note
sections.content: Articles are generally used with nouns. However, not every noun requires an article. The absence of an article in certain contexts is called the zero article.

examples.explanation: Books refers to books generally, so no article is needed.

lessons.title: Types of Articles
lessons.description: Learn about definite, indefinite and zero articles in English.

sections.heading: 1. The Three Articles
sections.content: English has three articles: A, An and The. They are divided into two main categories: indefinite articles and the definite article.

rules.name: Indefinite Articles
rules.description: A and An are used when referring to a non-specific singular countable noun.

rules.name: Definite Article
rules.description: The is used when referring to a specific or identifiable noun.
rules.example: The bird was sitting on a tree.

sections.heading: 2. Indefinite Articles – A and An
sections.content: A and An introduce a noun that is not specific or has not been identified yet.

rules.name: A
rules.description: Used before a word beginning with a consonant sound.
rules.example: A book, a car, a university.

rules.name: An
rules.description: Used before a word beginning with a vowel sound.
rules.example: An apple, an umbrella, an hour.

sections.heading: 3. Definite Article – The
sections.content: The identifies a particular person, place, animal or thing. It can be used with singular nouns, plural nouns and uncountable nouns when they are specific.

examples.explanation: We are referring to a particular teacher.

examples.sentence: The books on the table are mine.
examples.explanation: We are referring to specific books.

sections.heading: 4. Zero Article
sections.content: Sometimes we do not use any article before a noun. This is called the zero article.

examples.explanation: Dogs refers to animals in general, so no article is required.
Water is used in a general sense, so no article is required.

sections.heading: 5. Quick Comparison
sections.content: Remember the difference between these three forms:

examples.explanation: A particular pen known to the listener.
Pens in general; no article is needed.
